problem: Action-conditioned world models for embodied visual tracking can write the current action directly into the target-evidence state (causal hallucination), producing plausible futures but wrong semantics for tracking-oriented planning and target re-acquisition. Reactive trackers are myopic once the target is lost.
motivation: Tracking needs the robot to choose actions that preserve or recover future target observability and apparent scale, so it is a predictive decision problem. Action should influence target evidence only through ego-motion and the resulting observation change, not via a direct latent shortcut.
key_idea: Factor the latent state into target-evidence, robot, and observation branches and mask the transition so no direct edge runs from the current action to the target-evidence update, then plan with CEM-based MPC over rollouts.
insight: Structure of the action pathway matters, not just future prediction. Ablations show removing masking hurts re-acquisition most (0.61 vs 0.76) and lowers planning rank correlation (0.55 vs 0.68). Partial or shallow masking can be worse than none (leakage 0.37 for B vs 0.19 for A). The zero-Jacobian action-swap invariance and robot-motion-only checks show the pathway is selectively insensitive to action, while the observation branch stays action-sensitive.
method: Target-evidence token: H = [GroundingDINO confidence, normalized box area], an observation-derived summary of observability and apparent scale, with no privileged state at test time
Structured state: S = [H, Z (frozen SVD VAE latent), x (robot state from kinematic integration of action history)]

Causally masked transition: fixed order H_{l+1}=f_H(H,Z,x) with no action input; x_{l+1}=f_x(x,a); R_{l+1}=[x_{l+1}, W_a(a)] is the sole action carrier; Z_{l+1}=g(Z; R, H_{l+1}); implemented as a 6-block transformer

Diffusion training: DDPM noise-prediction loss over the shared next structured state, plus an auxiliary distance-aware BCE loss (weight 0.2) on the target-evidence branch using simulator in-range distance labels (train time only)

CEM MPC planning: T=10, N=128, K=16, M=4; value = visibility reward - |area - 0.5| distance penalty - action validity penalty - safety penalty (clearance 0.20 m); executes the first action in receding horizon
Diagnostics: Jacobian leakage, action-swap interventional invariance, robot-motion-only check, rollout fidelity, and planning-value rank correlation

setting.backbone: Structured diffusion transition transformer (6 blocks, hidden 512) + frozen SVD VAE + GroundingDINO detector, trained from scratch (3 seeds)
setting.training_data: EVT-Bench (48k trajectories, 1.92M one-step clips, 64 train scenes) and Habitat 3.0 (61k trajectories, 2.44M clips, 72 train scenes); scene-disjoint splits
setting.action_space: continuous velocity (linear v in R^2, angular omega), sampled by CEM
setting.simulator: EVT-Bench (Habitat-based) and Habitat 3.0; qualitative real-world demo
setting.privileged: none at test time (simulator relative distance used only as training-time auxiliary supervision)

numbers.backbone: CST-WM diffusion world model + CEM MPC

results: On EVT-Bench, CST-WM reaches SR 88.7 / TR 83.4 / CR 1.41, beating TrackVLA++ (86.0 / 81.0 / 2.10). On Habitat 3.0 it reaches F 0.53 / DRS 0.70 / ES 0.61 versus adapted NWM (0.41 / 0.61 / 0.49). It also leads in cross-dataset transfer and in re-acquisition under all four target-loss conditions, and Jacobian leakage falls to 0.001 (vs 0.112 for adapted NWM).
limitations: Depends on GroundingDINO detection quality; the area cue is only a proxy for distance, reliable roughly within 1-3 m
Real-world evidence is qualitative only; diffusion rollouts are costly (~150 ms per planning step, ~320 GPU-hours) and the distance loss needs simulator-only supervision
No persistent target identity under multiple similar distractors; the causal claim is structural, not full causal recovery
